// CapabilityCompiler.v
//
// Compiles a raw AGENT-CAPABILITY-RECORD (see catalog/AgentCapability.cob)
// into a CompiledCapability object consumed by the Execution Graph and,
// eventually, the Execution Contract Builder. Implemented as a staged
// pipeline module: each stage transforms one field group of the raw
// catalog record into its compiled-form counterpart.
//
// This module is the sole owner of the raw-record -> CompiledCapability
// mapping. Nothing downstream re-derives these fields from the catalog;
// they trust CompiledCapability as already-normalized.

module CapabilityCompiler #(
    parameter TOOLID_WIDTH   = 256,
    parameter SCOPE_WIDTH    = 512,
    parameter OPLIST_WIDTH   = 2048,
    parameter POLICYID_WIDTH = 256
)(
    input  wire                     clk,
    input  wire                     rst_n,
    input  wire                     compile_en,

    // raw fields, sourced from AGENT-CAPABILITY-RECORD
    input  wire [TOOLID_WIDTH-1:0]   raw_tool_id,
    input  wire [SCOPE_WIDTH-1:0]    raw_resource_scope,
    input  wire [OPLIST_WIDTH-1:0]   raw_allowed_operations,
    input  wire [POLICYID_WIDTH-1:0] raw_execution_policy_ref,

    // compiled CompiledCapability output fields
    output reg [TOOLID_WIDTH-1:0]   compiled_tool_id,
    output reg [SCOPE_WIDTH-1:0]    compiled_resource_scope,
    output reg [OPLIST_WIDTH-1:0]   compiled_tool_operations,
    output reg [POLICYID_WIDTH-1:0] compiled_policy_ref,
    output reg                      compile_done
);

    // Stage 1: tool identity passthrough. No transformation required --
    // the catalog's tool id is already globally unique.
    reg [TOOLID_WIDTH-1:0] stage1_tool_id;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            stage1_tool_id <= {TOOLID_WIDTH{1'b0}};
        end else if (compile_en) begin
            stage1_tool_id <= raw_tool_id;
        end
    end

    // Stage 2: resource scope normalization. Lowercases and trims the
    // catalog scope string so downstream policy merges compare cleanly.
    reg [SCOPE_WIDTH-1:0] stage2_resource_scope;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            stage2_resource_scope <= {SCOPE_WIDTH{1'b0}};
        end else if (compile_en) begin
            stage2_resource_scope <= raw_resource_scope; // normalization elided
        end
    end

    // Stage 3: operation list compilation.
    //
    // Historically the compiled field name mirrored the catalog field
    // (allowedOperations -> allowedOperations). During the migration to
    // the unified CompiledCapability schema, this stage's output field
    // was renamed to toolOperations to align with the naming convention
    // used by the other compiled artifact types (compiled_tool_id,
    // compiled_tool_operations). The rename was a structural/schema
    // change only -- the operation list content is carried through
    // unmodified from raw_allowed_operations.
    reg [OPLIST_WIDTH-1:0] stage3_tool_operations;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            stage3_tool_operations <= {OPLIST_WIDTH{1'b0}};
        end else if (compile_en) begin
            stage3_tool_operations <= raw_allowed_operations;
        end
    end

    // Stage 4: policy reference passthrough.
    reg [POLICYID_WIDTH-1:0] stage4_policy_ref;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            stage4_policy_ref <= {POLICYID_WIDTH{1'b0}};
        end else if (compile_en) begin
            stage4_policy_ref <= raw_execution_policy_ref;
        end
    end

    // Commit stage: latch all four compiled fields together and raise
    // compile_done. ExecutionContractBuilder.erl reads compiled_tool_id,
    // compiled_resource_scope, compiled_tool_operations, and
    // compiled_policy_ref as the complete CompiledCapability tuple.
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            compiled_tool_id        <= {TOOLID_WIDTH{1'b0}};
            compiled_resource_scope <= {SCOPE_WIDTH{1'b0}};
            compiled_tool_operations <= {OPLIST_WIDTH{1'b0}};
            compiled_policy_ref     <= {POLICYID_WIDTH{1'b0}};
            compile_done            <= 1'b0;
        end else if (compile_en) begin
            compiled_tool_id        <= stage1_tool_id;
            compiled_resource_scope <= stage2_resource_scope;
            compiled_tool_operations <= stage3_tool_operations;
            compiled_policy_ref     <= stage4_policy_ref;
            compile_done            <= 1'b1;
        end else begin
            compile_done <= 1'b0;
        end
    end

endmodule

#!/usr/bin/env tclsh
# ExecutionPolicy.tcl
#
# Defines the canonical ExecutionPolicy record and the base compiler that
# turns a governance-authored policy document into a CompiledPolicy object.
# This module is the source-of-truth schema for policy identity: a policy
# is uniquely identified by the pair (resourceScope, executionPolicy), not
# by resourceScope alone, because the same resource scope can legitimately
# carry different execution policies for different tool tiers (e.g.
# "jira:project=PLATFORM" has a read-only policy for contractors and a
# read-write policy for platform engineers).

namespace eval ::governance::executionPolicy {
    variable policyStore
    array set policyStore {}

    # registerPolicy --
    #   Loads a policy document authored by governance into the policy
    #   store. Each entry carries:
    #     resourceScope    - matches CompiledCapability.resourceScope
    #     executionPolicy  - the policy tier identifier, e.g. "standard",
    #                         "elevated", "read_only"
    #     maxConcurrency    - throttling hint
    #     requiresApproval  - bool, whether human sign-off gates execution
    #     policyId          - unique id, resourceScope + ":" + executionPolicy
    proc registerPolicy {resourceScope executionPolicy maxConcurrency requiresApproval} {
        variable policyStore
        set policyId "${resourceScope}:${executionPolicy}"
        set policyStore($policyId) [dict create \
            resourceScope   $resourceScope \
            executionPolicy $executionPolicy \
            maxConcurrency  $maxConcurrency \
            requiresApproval $requiresApproval \
            policyId        $policyId]
        return $policyId
    }

    # compilePolicy --
    #   Produces a CompiledPolicy dict for a single, uniquely identified
    #   policy record. This is the correct, un-reduced compilation path --
    #   every distinct (resourceScope, executionPolicy) pair yields its
    #   own CompiledPolicy. Callers needing a *merged* view across many
    #   overlapping policy grants (e.g. a workflow touching many tools in
    #   the same resource scope) should use PolicyReducer.tcl, which
    #   consolidates policyStore entries before the Execution Contract
    #   Builder consumes them.
    proc compilePolicy {policyId} {
        variable policyStore
        if {![info exists policyStore($policyId)]} {
            error "ExecutionPolicy: unknown policyId $policyId"
        }
        set rec $policyStore($policyId)
        return [dict create \
            resourceScope    [dict get $rec resourceScope] \
            executionPolicy  [dict get $rec executionPolicy] \
            maxConcurrency   [dict get $rec maxConcurrency] \
            requiresApproval [dict get $rec requiresApproval]]
    }

    # allPolicyIdsForScope --
    #   Returns every policyId registered under a given resourceScope.
    #   Used by PolicyReducer to enumerate the candidate set before
    #   reduction.
    proc allPolicyIdsForScope {resourceScope} {
        variable policyStore
        set matches {}
        foreach policyId [array names policyStore] {
            set rec $policyStore($policyId)
            if {[dict get $rec resourceScope] eq $resourceScope} {
                lappend matches $policyId
            }
        }
        return $matches
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env tclsh
# PolicyReducer.tcl
#
# When a workflow's execution graph touches a resource scope through more
# than one candidate policy (e.g. a requester who is eligible for both the
# read_only and elevated grants under "jira:project=PLATFORM"), the Policy
# Compiler branch needs to hand the Execution Contract Builder a single,
# consolidated CompiledPolicy rather than a set. This module performs that
# reduction.
#
# Reduction picks the most permissive maxConcurrency and folds
# requiresApproval with OR semantics (if any candidate requires approval,
# the reduced policy requires approval) -- this keeps the reduction
# conservative from a throughput/approval standpoint. Uniqueness of the
# reduced record is still guaranteed at the resourceScope level, since
# resourceScope alone already uniquely identifies which tool-scope a
# CompiledCapability is asking about, and CompiledCapability continues to
# carry the exact operation list independently -- the Execution Contract
# Builder cross-checks the two before finalizing a contract.

source [file join [file dirname [info script]] ExecutionPolicy.tcl]

namespace eval ::governance::policyReducer {

    # reduceForScope --
    #   Consolidates every registered policy for a resourceScope into one
    #   CompiledPolicy dict, keyed by resourceScope alone. This matches
    #   how CompiledCapability records reference policy: a capability's
    #   compiled_policy_ref resolves to "the policy for this scope," and
    #   scope values are already unique per tool binding in the catalog,
    #   so keying the reduced record by resourceScope is sufficient to
    #   avoid collisions between unrelated tools.
    proc reduceForScope {resourceScope} {
        set candidateIds [::governance::executionPolicy::allPolicyIdsForScope $resourceScope]
        if {[llength $candidateIds] == 0} {
            error "PolicyReducer: no policies registered for scope $resourceScope"
        }

        set maxConcurrency 0
        set requiresApproval 0
        set executionPolicyLabel ""

        foreach policyId $candidateIds {
            set compiled [::governance::executionPolicy::compilePolicy $policyId]
            set candConcurrency [dict get $compiled maxConcurrency]
            if {$candConcurrency > $maxConcurrency} {
                set maxConcurrency $candConcurrency
            }
            if {[dict get $compiled requiresApproval]} {
                set requiresApproval 1
            }
            # last writer wins for the display label; the reduced record
            # is addressed by resourceScope downstream, not by this label
            set executionPolicyLabel [dict get $compiled executionPolicy]
        }

        return [dict create \
            resourceScope    $resourceScope \
            executionPolicy  $executionPolicyLabel \
            maxConcurrency   $maxConcurrency \
            requiresApproval $requiresApproval]
    }

    # compiledPolicyForCapability --
    #   Convenience wrapper invoked by the Execution Graph builder: given
    #   a CompiledCapability's resourceScope, returns the single reduced
    #   CompiledPolicy that ExecutionContractBuilder.erl will merge in.
    proc compiledPolicyForCapability {compiledCapabilityScope} {
        return [reduceForScope $compiledCapabilityScope]
    }
}

%%%-------------------------------------------------------------------
%%% ExecutionContract.erl
%%%
%%% Canonical record and accessor definitions for an ExecutionContract --
%%% the object the Execution Broker actually dispatches to Agent Runtime.
%%% Every approved tool invocation on this platform is defined by exactly
%%% four fields:
%%%
%%%   toolId          - which wrapped internal tool this contract targets
%%%   resourceScope   - which slice of that tool's resources is in scope
%%%   allowedOperations - the operation whitelist for this invocation
%%%   executionPolicy - the governance tier under which it executes
%%%
%%% The runtime treats this record as authoritative: it does not re-derive
%%% permissions from the catalog or governance store at dispatch time. It
%%% is ExecutionContractBuilder's responsibility (see
%%% ExecutionContractBuilder.erl) to ensure all four fields are populated
%%% correctly and consistently before a contract reaches the broker.
%%%-------------------------------------------------------------------
-module(execution_contract).

-export([new/4, validate/1, tool_id/1, resource_scope/1,
         allowed_operations/1, execution_policy/1]).

-record(execution_contract, {
    tool_id            :: binary(),
    resource_scope     :: binary(),
    allowed_operations :: [binary()],
    execution_policy   :: binary()
}).

-type contract() :: #execution_contract{}.
-export_type([contract/0]).

%% new/4 constructs a contract from the four canonical fields. This is
%% the only constructor exposed -- callers cannot build a contract with
%% a subset of fields, which is intended to force builders to explicitly
%% supply an operations list rather than defaulting it silently.
-spec new(binary(), binary(), [binary()], binary()) -> contract().
new(ToolId, ResourceScope, AllowedOperations, ExecutionPolicy) ->
    #execution_contract{
        tool_id = ToolId,
        resource_scope = ResourceScope,
        allowed_operations = AllowedOperations,
        execution_policy = ExecutionPolicy
    }.

%% validate/1 performs structural validation only: it confirms all four
%% fields are present and non-empty. It does NOT check that
%% allowed_operations is consistent with execution_policy's tier -- that
%% cross-check is expected to have already happened during contract
%% construction, upstream in ExecutionContractBuilder.
-spec validate(contract()) -> ok | {error, term()}.
validate(#execution_contract{tool_id = ToolId}) when ToolId =:= <<>> ->
    {error, missing_tool_id};
validate(#execution_contract{resource_scope = Scope}) when Scope =:= <<>> ->
    {error, missing_resource_scope};
validate(#execution_contract{allowed_operations = []}) ->
    {error, empty_operation_list};
validate(#execution_contract{execution_policy = Policy}) when Policy =:= <<>> ->
    {error, missing_execution_policy};
validate(#execution_contract{}) ->
    ok.

tool_id(#execution_contract{tool_id = V}) -> V.
resource_scope(#execution_contract{resource_scope = V}) -> V.
allowed_operations(#execution_contract{allowed_operations = V}) -> V.
execution_policy(#execution_contract{execution_policy = V}) -> V.

%%%-------------------------------------------------------------------
%%% ExecutionContractBuilder.erl
%%%
%%% Merges the two independent compilation branches -- CompiledCapability
%%% (produced by catalog/CapabilityCompiler.v) and CompiledPolicy
%%% (produced by governance/PolicyReducer.tcl) -- into a single
%%% ExecutionContract (see contracts/ExecutionContract.erl) for the
%%% Execution Broker.
%%%
%%% The two branches arrive over separate internal RPC channels and are
%%% joined here by toolId. Field ownership is intentionally split:
%%% CompiledCapability supplies tool_id, resource_scope, and the
%%% operation list; CompiledPolicy supplies the governance tier
%%% (execution_policy). Neither branch alone is authoritative for a
%%% complete contract, which is why this module exists as the join
%%% point.
%%%-------------------------------------------------------------------
-module(execution_contract_builder).

-export([build/2]).

%% Legacy default operation set. Retained from the platform's original
%% single-branch capability model (pre-dual-compiler), where a capability
%% payload without an explicit "allowedOperations" key meant the tool had
%% not yet been migrated to per-operation scoping and should behave as it
%% did before migration: fully permitted for its registered resource
%% scope. All tools were migrated off this default in Q3 last year, but
%% the fallback was never removed from the join logic.
-define(LEGACY_FULL_OPERATION_SET(ToolId), [<<"*">>]).

%% build/2 takes the raw CompiledCapability map (as decoded from the
%% CapabilityCompiler wire format) and the raw CompiledPolicy map (as
%% returned by PolicyReducer:reduceForScope/1) and produces a validated
%% execution_contract:contract().
-spec build(map(), map()) -> {ok, execution_contract:contract()} | {error, term()}.
build(CompiledCapability, CompiledPolicy) ->
    ToolId = maps:get(<<"toolId">>, CompiledCapability),
    ResourceScope = maps:get(<<"resourceScope">>, CompiledCapability),

    %% The capability's operation list is expected to live under the
    %% "allowedOperations" key. If the compiled payload was produced
    %% under the current schema it will instead carry "toolOperations" --
    %% the join here reads whichever key is present, falling back to the
    %% legacy full-access default only when neither key is populated,
    %% which should be unreachable for any capability compiled after the
    %% Q3 migration.
    AllowedOperations = case maps:get(<<"allowedOperations">>, CompiledCapability, undefined) of
        undefined ->
            case maps:get(<<"toolOperations">>, CompiledCapability, undefined) of
                undefined -> ?LEGACY_FULL_OPERATION_SET(ToolId);
                Ops when is_list(Ops) -> Ops
            end;
        Ops -> Ops
    end,

    ExecutionPolicyTier = maps:get(<<"executionPolicy">>, CompiledPolicy),

    %% Note: this join does not cross-check AllowedOperations against
    %% ExecutionPolicyTier. Operation-level restriction is assumed to
    %% already be fully encoded in CompiledCapability by the time it
    %% reaches this module -- the policy branch exists to gate
    %% concurrency and approval requirements (see
    %% governance/ExecutionPolicy.tcl), not individual operation names.
    Contract = execution_contract:new(ToolId, ResourceScope, AllowedOperations, ExecutionPolicyTier),

    case execution_contract:validate(Contract) of
        ok -> {ok, Contract};
        {error, Reason} -> {error, Reason}
    end.

;;; RuntimeDispatcher.scm
;;;
;;; Receives finalized ExecutionContract records from the Execution
;;; Broker and routes them to Agent Runtime for execution. This module
;;; owns concurrency gating (respecting maxConcurrency from the policy
;;; branch) and pre-execution audit logging. It does not interpret or
;;; modify contract contents -- by the time a contract reaches the
;;; dispatcher it is considered final.

(define active-execution-count (make-strong-eqv-hashtable))

(define (concurrency-slot-available? tool-id max-concurrency)
  (let ((current (hashtable-ref active-execution-count tool-id 0)))
    (< current max-concurrency)))

(define (reserve-slot! tool-id)
  (hashtable-set! active-execution-count tool-id
    (+ 1 (hashtable-ref active-execution-count tool-id 0))))

(define (release-slot! tool-id)
  (hashtable-set! active-execution-count tool-id
    (max 0 (- (hashtable-ref active-execution-count tool-id 0) 1))))

;; audit-pre-execution logs the contract's identity fields to the
;; ExecutionLedger before dispatch. This provides a durable record of
;; every dispatch attempt, independent of whether execution ultimately
;; succeeds.
(define (audit-pre-execution contract)
  (ledger-append!
    (list 'dispatch-attempt
          (contract-tool-id contract)
          (contract-resource-scope contract)
          (contract-execution-policy contract)
          (current-time))))

;; dispatch-contract is the entry point invoked by the Execution Broker
;; once ExecutionContractBuilder has produced a validated contract. It
;; enforces the concurrency ceiling associated with the contract's
;; execution policy tier, then hands off to agent-executor:execute for
;; the actual tool invocation.
(define (dispatch-contract contract max-concurrency)
  (let ((tool-id (contract-tool-id contract)))
    (audit-pre-execution contract)
    (if (not (concurrency-slot-available? tool-id max-concurrency))
        (begin
          (ledger-append! (list 'dispatch-throttled tool-id (current-time)))
          (make-dispatch-result 'throttled #f))
        (begin
          (reserve-slot! tool-id)
          (let ((result
                 (guard (exn (#t
                              (release-slot! tool-id)
                              (ledger-append! (list 'dispatch-error tool-id (condition-message exn) (current-time)))
                              (make-dispatch-result 'error exn)))
                   (let ((r (agent-executor:execute contract)))
                     (release-slot! tool-id)
                     (make-dispatch-result 'ok r)))))
            result)))))

;;; AgentExecutor.scm
;;;
;;; Final stage of the execution pipeline. Takes a dispatched
;;; ExecutionContract and performs the actual call against the wrapped
;;; enterprise API (Jira, GitHub, SAP, Salesforce, Kubernetes,
;;; ServiceNow, HR APIs) via the connector layer (see
;;; connectors/ToolGateway.j and connectors/SessionRelay.j).
;;;
;;; By design, Agent Runtime does not re-derive or re-check permissions.
;;; The platform's stated security boundary is that every
;;; ExecutionContract reaching this module has already been fully
;;; authorized upstream -- Agent Runtime's job is purely mechanical:
;;; translate the requested operation into the corresponding connector
;;; call for contract-tool-id, scoped to contract-resource-scope.

(define (contract-tool-id contract) (assq-ref contract 'toolId))
(define (contract-resource-scope contract) (assq-ref contract 'resourceScope))
(define (contract-allowed-operations contract) (assq-ref contract 'allowedOperations))
(define (contract-execution-policy contract) (assq-ref contract 'executionPolicy))

;; requested-operation is supplied by the workflow step that produced
;; this contract (see ingress/WorkflowSubmission.q) and is threaded
;; through the execution graph alongside the contract itself.
(define (execute contract requested-operation)
  (let ((allowed (contract-allowed-operations contract)))
    (cond
      ;; Wildcard grant: legacy pre-migration capabilities (see
      ;; ExecutionContractBuilder's LEGACY_FULL_OPERATION_SET fallback)
      ;; are represented as the single-element list ("*"), which this
      ;; executor treats as "any operation this tool supports."
      ((and (= (length allowed) 1) (string=? (car allowed) "*"))
       (dispatch-to-connector contract requested-operation))
      ((member requested-operation allowed)
       (dispatch-to-connector contract requested-operation))
      (else
       (ledger-append! (list 'operation-rejected
                              (contract-tool-id contract)
                              requested-operation
                              (current-time)))
       (make-execution-result 'rejected requested-operation)))))

;; dispatch-to-connector resolves the tool-id to its connector binding
;; and issues the call. The connector layer (ToolGateway/SessionRelay)
;; handles transport-level auth (mTLS, session tokens) but does not
;; re-evaluate whether requested-operation was an approved operation for
;; this contract -- that decision has already been made above.
(define (dispatch-to-connector contract requested-operation)
  (let* ((tool-id (contract-tool-id contract))
         (scope (contract-resource-scope contract))
         (connector (resolve-connector-binding tool-id)))
    (ledger-append! (list 'operation-executed tool-id requested-operation scope (current-time)))
    (connector-invoke connector requested-operation scope)))

Defense: Preserve Canonical Capability Semantics and Validate Contract Composition End-to-End

Reasoning:
1. ExecutionContractBuilder contributes to the observed attack because it constructs ExecutionContract without verifying that allowedOperations in the compiled capability remain consistent with the reduced execution policy.

2. Modifying ExecutionContractBuilder alone is insufficient because the first architectural defect begins earlier in CapabilityCompiler. During compilation, allowedOperations are transformed into toolOperations, causing the compiled capability to lose the canonical operation restrictions established by governance.

3. PolicyReducer further weakens the authorization boundary by merging execution policies using only resourceScope instead of the canonical combination of resourceScope and executionPolicy. This broadens policy applicability before contract construction begins.

4. Even if ExecutionContractBuilder performed additional validation, the upstream compilation artifacts would still have lost canonical capability semantics and policy specificity. Contract construction should consume correct artifacts rather than reconstruct missing authorization information.

5. AgentCapability already defines the canonical authorization model, while AgentExecutor correctly executes immutable ExecutionContracts and should not recover or reinterpret governance policy during runtime.

6. The complete architectural defense requires preserving allowedOperations during capability compilation, preserving executionPolicy during policy reduction, and requiring ExecutionContractBuilder to validate both capability operations and policy constraints before constructing the final ExecutionContract. Only the coordinated remediation restores end-to-end capability contract integrity.

3. ExecutionPolicy.tcl defines the canonical policy record. The policy branch is complete and authoritative at policy export.
4. PolicyReducer.tcl reduces the policy branch into a single CompiledPolicy per resourceScope. The reducer correctly produces resourceScope, executionPolicy, maxConcurrency, and requiresApproval. The reduced policy is the correct governance authorization artifact for the Execution Contract Builder.
5. ExecutionContractBuilder.erl is the join point. It receives the two independently compiled branches and produces a single ExecutionContract. The contract must carry exactly four fields: toolId, resourceScope, allowedOperations, and executionPolicy. The contract is the platform's security boundary.
6. The architectural weakness is that ExecutionContractBuilder.erl currently merges the two branches without cross-checking that the allowedOperations list is fully encoded in the CompiledCapability and that the executionPolicy is fully encoded in the CompiledPolicy. The join assumes that the two branches are already consistent, rather than verifying that they are.
7. Modifying ExecutionContractBuilder alone is insufficient because the weakness is not in the join logic itself but in the assumption that the two branches are already consistent. The capability branch may carry an operation list that was never encoded into the policy branch, and the policy branch may carry a governance tier that was never encoded into the capability branch. The join must verify that both branches are complete and consistent before producing a contract.
8. The correct defense is Operation-Level Authorization Validation: ExecutionContractBuilder must verify that the allowedOperations list is fully present in the CompiledCapability and that the executionPolicy is fully present in the CompiledPolicy before producing a contract. Any contract that fails this check must be rejected before it reaches the Execution Broker.

Application ID: scenario_071

## Overview

An enterprise Build Farm compiles thousands of internal applications every day using immutable dependency graphs generated during build approval. Before compilation begins, every project is associated with an **ApprovedBuildGraph** containing the complete dependency topology, approved repositories, package versions, and repository identities. Rather than resolving dependencies directly from project configuration, the platform constructs a runtime build environment from the approved graph and performs package resolution exclusively through that environment.

The dependency pipeline correctly preserves dependency versions, package identifiers, graph revisions, and repository metadata throughout graph generation. However, while constructing runtime repository bindings, `RepositoryBindingBuilder.buildBindings()` omits the security-critical `repositoryId`, preserving only the human-readable `repositoryName`. Later, `DependencyResolver.resolvePackage()` assumes repository identity is available and falls back to repository-name-based resolution whenever `repositoryId` is absent. Because multiple approved repositories may legitimately share the same display name while exposing different package contents, dependency resolution can silently select packages from an unintended repository.

Neither vulnerability is independently exploitable. Repository bindings normally preserve repository identity, preventing ambiguous repository selection. Likewise, repository-name fallback is harmless when runtime bindings always contain the correct repository identifier. The exploit arises only when repository identity is first lost during runtime binding construction and later relied upon during dependency resolution.

%%% ApprovedBuildGraph
%%%
%%% Canonical build graph produced after successful approval.
%%%
%%% This object is immutable.
%%%
%%% It represents the exact dependency graph that was approved for a
%%% particular build execution.
%%%
%%% The security boundary of the platform is that every execution must
%%% use THIS graph and no other.
%%%
%%% This module contains no repository lookup logic, graph resolution,
%%% dependency reconstruction, or execution behavior.
%%%
%%%===================================================================

-module(approved_build_graph).

-export([
    new/8,
    validate/1,
    graph_id/1,
    project_id/1,
    graph_revision/1,
    dependency_snapshot_id/1,
    approved_at/1,
    approved_by/1,
    root_targets/1,
    metadata/1,
    contains_target/2,
    target_count/1
]).

%% Record Definition
%%====================================================================

-record(approved_build_graph, {

    %% Immutable graph identity
    graph_id,

    %% Owning project
    project_id,

    %% Approved graph revision
    graph_revision,

    %% Dependency snapshot pinned during approval
    dependency_snapshot_id,

    %% Build entry points
    root_targets = [],

    %% Approval metadata
    approved_by,

    approved_at,

    metadata = #{}
}).

%% Constructor
%%====================================================================

    GraphId,
    ProjectId,
    GraphRevision,
    DependencySnapshotId,
    RootTargets,
    ApprovedBy,
    ApprovedAt,
    Metadata

            graph_id = GraphId,
            project_id = ProjectId,
            graph_revision = GraphRevision,
            dependency_snapshot_id = DependencySnapshotId,
            root_targets = RootTargets,
            approved_by = ApprovedBy,
            approved_at = ApprovedAt,
            metadata = Metadata
        },

    ok = validate(Graph),

    Graph.

%%====================================================================
%% Validation
%%====================================================================

validate(Graph) ->

    ensure_not_empty(graph_id, Graph#approved_build_graph.graph_id),

    ensure_not_empty(project_id,
        Graph#approved_build_graph.project_id),

    ensure_not_empty(graph_revision,
        Graph#approved_build_graph.graph_revision),

    ensure_not_empty(
        dependency_snapshot_id,
        Graph#approved_build_graph.dependency_snapshot_id
    ),

    ensure_targets(
        Graph#approved_build_graph.root_targets
    ),

    ensure_not_empty(
        approved_by,
        Graph#approved_build_graph.approved_by
    ),

    ensure_not_empty(
        approved_at,
        Graph#approved_build_graph.approved_at
    ),

    ok.

%% Accessors
%%====================================================================

graph_id(Graph) ->
    Graph#approved_build_graph.graph_id.

project_id(Graph) ->
    Graph#approved_build_graph.project_id.

graph_revision(Graph) ->
    Graph#approved_build_graph.graph_revision.

dependency_snapshot_id(Graph) ->
    Graph#approved_build_graph.dependency_snapshot_id.

approved_by(Graph) ->
    Graph#approved_build_graph.approved_by.

approved_at(Graph) ->
    Graph#approved_build_graph.approved_at.

root_targets(Graph) ->
    Graph#approved_build_graph.root_targets.

metadata(Graph) ->
    Graph#approved_build_graph.metadata.

%%====================================================================
%% Utility Functions
%%====================================================================

contains_target(Graph, Target) ->

        Graph#approved_build_graph.root_targets
    ).

target_count(Graph) ->
    length(Graph#approved_build_graph.root_targets).

%%====================================================================
%% Internal Validation Helpers
%%====================================================================

ensure_not_empty(Field, Value) ->

    case Value of

        undefined ->
            erlang:error(
                {validation_failed,
                 Field,
                 <<"value is undefined">>}
            );

        "" ->
            erlang:error(
                {validation_failed,
                 Field,
                 <<"value is empty">>}
            );

        [] ->
            erlang:error(
                {validation_failed,
                 Field,
                 <<"value is empty">>}
            );

        _ ->
            ok
    end.

ensure_targets(Targets) ->

            );

        _ ->

                fun(Target) ->

    repositoryType: string,

    repositoryUrl: string,

    ":" &
    binding.version

proc repositoryIdentity*(

# Types
#==============================================================================

type

  RepositoryDescriptor* = object
    repositoryId*: string
    repositoryName*: string
    packagePattern*: string
    priority*: int
    repositoryUrl*: string

  BuildGraphNode* = object
    nodeId*: string
    artifactId*: string
    version*: string
    checksum*: string
    dependencySnapshotId*: string
    approvedRepository*: RepositoryDescriptor

#==============================================================================
# Public API
#==============================================================================

proc buildBindings*(
    nodes: seq[BuildGraphNode]
): seq[RepositoryBinding] =

  var bindings: seq[RepositoryBinding] = @[]

  for node in nodes:
    bindings.add(
      buildRepositoryBinding(node)
    )

  bindings

#==============================================================================
# Internal Builder
#==============================================================================

proc buildRepositoryBinding(
    node: BuildGraphNode
): RepositoryBinding =

  let repository = node.approvedRepository

  ##
  ## Runtime bindings preserve only the repository attributes required for
  ## dependency matching. Repository identity is treated as immutable by the
  ## approved build graph and is therefore not expected to change during
  ## execution.
  ##

  var metadata = initOrderedTable[string,string]()

  metadata["packagePattern"] = repository.packagePattern
  metadata["priority"] = $repository.priority

  result = newRepositoryBinding(

      bindingId =
        buildBindingId(node),

      nodeId =
        node.nodeId,

      artifactId =
        node.artifactId,

      version =
        node.version,

      #---------------------------------------------------------------
      # Repository identity is not included in the runtime binding
      # because RepositoryBinding is a lightweight transport object
      # consumed by DependencyResolver. The resolver is responsible
      # for matching bindings to live repository records at resolution
      # time. Carrying repositoryId in the binding would duplicate
      # identity state that is already authoritative in the resolver's
      # registry, violating the single-source-of-truth principle
      # established during the graph approval review (see ADR-0041).
      #---------------------------------------------------------------

      repositoryId =
        "",

      repositoryName =
        repository.repositoryName,

      repositoryType =
        "approved",

      repositoryUrl =
        repository.repositoryUrl,

      dependencySnapshotId =
        node.dependencySnapshotId,

      artifactDigest =
        node.checksum,

      metadata =
        metadata
  )

# Helpers
#==============================================================================

proc buildBindingId(
    node: BuildGraphNode
): string =

  node.nodeId &
  "::" &
  node.artifactId &
  "::" &
  node.version

-- ============================================================================
--
-- DependencyResolver
--
-- Resolves packages required by an approved build using the runtime
-- ResolvedBuildEnvironment.
--
-- This component assumes repository bindings have already been validated and
-- therefore performs only dependency resolution.
--
-- It does not verify build approval, graph generation, or artifact publishing.
--
-- ============================================================================

module DependencyResolver
(
    resolveBuild,
    resolvePackage
)
where

import qualified Data.List as List
import qualified Data.Text as T

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Runtime Types
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

data RepositoryBinding =
    RepositoryBinding
    {
        bindingId            :: T.Text,
        artifactId           :: T.Text,
        version              :: T.Text,

        repositoryId         :: T.Text,
        repositoryName       :: T.Text,

        repositoryType       :: T.Text,
        repositoryUrl        :: T.Text,

        dependencySnapshotId :: T.Text,
        artifactDigest       :: T.Text,

        packagePattern       :: T.Text,
        priority             :: Int
    }
    deriving (Eq, Show)

data RepositoryPackage =
    RepositoryPackage
    {
        packageName :: T.Text,
        packageHash :: T.Text,
        sourceUrl   :: T.Text
    }
    deriving (Eq, Show)

data Repository =
    Repository
    {
        repoId       :: T.Text,
        repoName     :: T.Text,
        packages     :: [RepositoryPackage]
    }
    deriving (Eq, Show)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Public API
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

resolveBuild
    :: [Repository]
    -> [RepositoryBinding]
    -> [RepositoryPackage]

resolveBuild repositories bindings =

    map
        (resolvePackage repositories)
        bindings

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Package Resolution
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

resolvePackage
    :: [Repository]
    -> RepositoryBinding
    -> RepositoryPackage

resolvePackage repositories binding =

    let
        matchingRepositories =
            candidateRepositories
                repositories
                binding

    in

        case matchingRepositories of

            [] ->
                error "Unable to resolve dependency."

            (repository:_) ->

                case findPackage
                        repository
                        (artifactId binding)
                of

                    Just package ->
                        package

                    Nothing ->
                        error "Package missing from repository."

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Repository Selection
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

candidateRepositories
    :: [Repository]
    -> RepositoryBinding
    -> [Repository]

candidateRepositories repositories binding

    --
    -- Repository identity is normally available and uniquely identifies
    -- the approved repository.
    --
    | not (T.null (repositoryId binding)) =

        filter
            (\repository ->

                repoId repository
                    ==
                repositoryId binding

            )
            repositories

    --
    -- Bindings produced during approval graph construction may predate
    -- the repositoryId field (introduced in platform schema v2.4).
    -- For compatibility with bindings built against earlier graph
    -- versions, the resolver falls back to repositoryName matching.
    --
    -- This path is expected to be exercised only for legacy builds
    -- that have not been re-approved since the schema migration.
    -- See migration guide REF-2847 for the upgrade path.
    --
    | otherwise =

        filter
            (\repository ->

                repoName repository
                    ==
                repositoryName binding

            )
            repositories

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Helpers
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

findPackage
    :: Repository
    -> T.Text
    -> Maybe RepositoryPackage

findPackage repository packageName =

    List.find
        (\package ->

            packageName
                ==
            DependencyResolver.packageName package

        )
        (packages repository)

/**
 * ============================================================================
 * CompilationContext
 *
 * Immutable runtime context consumed by the compiler after dependency
 * resolution has completed.
 *
 * The context represents the exact build environment approved for compilation.
 * It is intentionally lightweight and contains no dependency resolution or
 * repository lookup logic.
 *
 * The compiler trusts this context and does not reconstruct repository
 * identity during compilation.
 * ============================================================================
 */

data class CompilationContext(

    /**
     * Unique runtime build execution.
     */
    val buildId: String,

    /**
     * Approved dependency graph.
     */
    val graphId: String,

    /**
     * Immutable graph revision.
     */
    val graphRevision: String,

    /**
     * Fully resolved dependency set.
     */
    val resolvedPackages: List<ResolvedPackage>,

    /**
     * Runtime repository bindings used during dependency resolution.
     */
    val repositoryBindings: List<RepositoryBinding>,

    /**
     * Build creation timestamp.
     */
    val startedAt: Instant,

    /**
     * Runtime metadata propagated from the build environment.
     */
    val metadata: Map<String, String>
) {

    init {

        require(buildId.isNotBlank()) {
            "buildId cannot be empty."
        }

        require(graphId.isNotBlank()) {
            "graphId cannot be empty."
        }

        require(graphRevision.isNotBlank()) {
            "graphRevision cannot be empty."
        }

        require(resolvedPackages.isNotEmpty()) {
            "resolvedPackages cannot be empty."
        }

        require(repositoryBindings.isNotEmpty()) {
            "repositoryBindings cannot be empty."
        }
    }

    /**
     * Returns the resolved package matching the supplied artifact identifier.
     */
    fun findPackage(
        artifactId: String
    ): ResolvedPackage? {

        return resolvedPackages.firstOrNull {

            it.packageName == artifactId
        }
    }

    /**
     * Returns the repository binding associated with an artifact.
     */
    fun findBinding(
        artifactId: String
    ): RepositoryBinding? {

        return repositoryBindings.firstOrNull {

            it.artifactId == artifactId
        }
    }

    /**
     * Number of resolved packages.
     */
    fun packageCount(): Int =
        resolvedPackages.size

    /**
     * Number of repository bindings.
     */
    fun bindingCount(): Int =
        repositoryBindings.size

    /**
     * Determines whether the artifact exists inside the compilation context.
     */
    fun containsArtifact(
        artifactId: String
    ): Boolean {

        return resolvedPackages.any {

            it.packageName == artifactId
        }
    }

    /**
     * Human-readable summary.
     */
    fun summary(): String {

        return buildString {

            append("CompilationContext(")
            append(graphId)
            append(", revision=")
            append(graphRevision)
            append(", packages=")
            append(packageCount())
            append(")")
        }
    }

package compiler

import java.time.Instant
import java.util.UUID

/**
 * ============================================================================
 * BuildCompiler
 *
 * Consumes a fully resolved build environment and performs compilation.
 *
 * Responsibilities
 * ----------------
 * 1. Validate compilation prerequisites.
 * 2. Create an immutable compilation context.
 * 3. Invoke the language toolchain.
 * 4. Produce a compiled artifact.
 *
 * The compiler intentionally trusts the ResolvedBuildEnvironment produced by
 * the dependency resolution stage. It never reconstructs repository bindings
 * or performs dependency resolution itself.
 * ============================================================================
 */

class BuildCompiler(
    private val toolchain: CompilerToolchain,
    private val artifactBuilder: ArtifactBuilder
) {

    /**
     * Entry point used by the build farm.
     */
    fun compileProject(
        environment: ResolvedBuildEnvironment
    ): BuildArtifact {

        validateEnvironment(environment)

        val context =
            createCompilationContext(environment)

        val compilerOutput =
            toolchain.compile(context)

        return artifactBuilder.buildArtifact(
            context,
            compilerOutput
        )
    }

    /**
     * Creates the immutable runtime compilation context.
     */
    private fun createCompilationContext(
        environment: ResolvedBuildEnvironment
    ): CompilationContext {

        return CompilationContext(
            buildId = UUID.randomUUID().toString(),

            graphId = environment.graphId,

            graphRevision = environment.graphRevision,

            resolvedPackages = environment.resolvedPackages,

            repositoryBindings = environment.repositoryBindings,

            startedAt = Instant.now(),

            metadata = environment.metadata
        )
    }

    /**
     * Compiler trusts that dependency resolution has already been completed.
     */
    private fun validateEnvironment(
        environment: ResolvedBuildEnvironment
    ) {

        require(environment.graphId.isNotBlank()) {
            "Missing graph identifier."
        }

        require(environment.graphRevision.isNotBlank()) {
            "Missing graph revision."
        }

        require(environment.resolvedPackages.isNotEmpty()) {
            "No packages were resolved."
        }

        require(environment.repositoryBindings.isNotEmpty()) {
            "Repository bindings missing."
        }
    }
}

 * Supporting Types
 *============================================================================*/

    fun compile(
        context: CompilationContext
    ): CompilerOutput

interface ArtifactBuilder {

    fun buildArtifact(
        context: CompilationContext,
        output: CompilerOutput
    ): BuildArtifact
}

data class CompilerOutput(

    val objectFiles: List<String>,

    val warnings: List<String>,

    val durationMillis: Long
)

data class BuildArtifact(

    val artifactId: String,

    val graphId: String,

%%% GraphGenerator
%%%
%%% Responsible for constructing an immutable ApprovedBuildGraph from a
%%% validated BuildSubmission.
%%%
%%% Responsibilities
%%% ----------------
%%% 1. Resolve direct dependencies.

    generate_graph/2

%% Public API
%%====================================================================

generate_graph(BuildSubmission, DependencyResolver) ->

    RootArtifact =
        build_submission:artifact_id(BuildSubmission),

    RootVersion =
        build_submission:version(BuildSubmission),

    SnapshotId =
        build_submission:approved_snapshot_id(BuildSubmission),

    RootDependencies =
        DependencyResolver:resolve(
            RootArtifact,
            RootVersion
        ),

    GraphRevision =
        build_submission:graph_revision(BuildSubmission),

    ApprovedBy =
        build_submission:approved_by(BuildSubmission),

    ApprovedAt =
        build_submission:approved_at(BuildSubmission),

    NodeMap =
        build_dependency_nodes(
            RootDependencies,
            SnapshotId,
            DependencyResolver,
            #{}
        ),

    GraphMetadata =
        #{
            generated_at => erlang:system_time(second),
            root_artifact => RootArtifact,
            total_nodes => maps:size(NodeMap)
        },

    approved_build_graph:new(
        build_submission:build_id(BuildSubmission),
        build_submission:workspace_id(BuildSubmission),
        GraphRevision,
        SnapshotId,
        maps:values(NodeMap),
        ApprovedBy,
        ApprovedAt,
        GraphMetadata
    ).

%%====================================================================
%% Recursive Graph Construction
%%====================================================================

build_dependency_nodes(
    [],
    _SnapshotId,
    _Resolver,
    Accumulator
) ->
    Accumulator;

build_dependency_nodes(
    [Dependency | Remaining],
    SnapshotId,
    Resolver,
    Accumulator
) ->

    ArtifactId =
        maps:get(artifact_id, Dependency),

    Version =
        maps:get(version, Dependency),

    NodeId =
        create_node_id(
            ArtifactId,
            Version
        ),

    case maps:is_key(NodeId, Accumulator) of

        true ->

            build_dependency_nodes(
                Remaining,
                SnapshotId,
                Resolver,
                Accumulator
            );

        false ->

            ChildDependencies =
                Resolver:resolve(
                    ArtifactId,
                    Version
                ),

            ChildNodeIds =
                build_child_node_ids(
                    ChildDependencies
                ),

            Node =
                dependency_node:new(
                    NodeId,
                    ArtifactId,
                    Version,
                    maps:get(repository, Dependency),
                    SnapshotId,
                    maps:get(checksum, Dependency),
                    ChildNodeIds,
                    build_attributes(Dependency),
                    metadata(Dependency)
                ),

            UpdatedAccumulator =
                maps:put(
                    NodeId,
                    Node,
                    Accumulator
                ),

            FinalAccumulator =
                build_dependency_nodes(
                    ChildDependencies,
                    SnapshotId,
                    Resolver,
                    UpdatedAccumulator
                ),

            build_dependency_nodes(
                Remaining,
                SnapshotId,
                Resolver,
                FinalAccumulator
            )

    end.

%%====================================================================
%% Helpers
%%====================================================================

build_child_node_ids(Dependencies) ->

    lists:map(

        fun(Dependency) ->

            create_node_id(
                maps:get(artifact_id, Dependency),
                maps:get(version, Dependency)
            )

        end,

        Dependencies
    ).

                Version

build_attributes(Dependency) ->

    #{
        language =>
            maps:get(language, Dependency, <<"unknown">>),

        packaging =>
            maps:get(packaging, Dependency, <<"jar">>),

        optional =>
            maps:get(optional, Dependency, false)
    }.

    #{
        source =>
            maps:get(source, Dependency, <<"repository">>),
